activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Eigenvectors of a 3x3 Matrix in the General Case

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 0 \\ -3 & -6 & 0 \\ -3 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. What are the dimensions of the eigenspaces ${V}_{0}$ and ${V}_{-3}$ corresponding to eigenvalues $\lambda =0$ and $\lambda =-3$ of $A$, respectively?
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we write down the characteristic equation $\text{det}(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(A-\lambda I)=0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 6 & 0 \\ -3 & -6-\lambda  & 0 \\ -3 & -6 & -\lambda \end{aligned}|=0 \\ -\lambda |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 6 \\ -3 & -6-\lambda \end{aligned}|=0 \\ \lambda ((3-\lambda )(-6-\lambda )+18)=0 \\ \lambda (-18+3\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+18)=0 \\ \lambda (3\lambda +{\lambda }^{2})=0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}(3+\lambda )=0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=0$ (double root) and ${\lambda }_{3}=-3$ (simple root).

Let's now consider the eigenspaces corresponding to each eigenvector:

- First, we consider $\lambda =-3.$ Since ${V}_{-3}$ corresponds to a simple root, we obtain 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-3})=1.
$$

- Then, we consider $\lambda =0,$ which is a repeated root of the characteristic equation. To find the dimension of ${V}_{0},$ we row-reduce the matrix $(A-0I)\text{x}=0:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 0 \\ -3 & -6 & 0 \\ -3 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}]-0[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 0 \\ -3 & -6 & 0 \\ -3 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =0.$ Therefore, 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{0})=2.
$$
